description: Every case MUST be rejected with exactly `expect_error`. A decoder that accepts any of these, or returns a different error code, fails conformance. Rejection MUST be silent: no peer instance, no UI, no payload in logs.
validation_order_note: Order is normative so that multi-fault frames produce a deterministic error on both platforms. See the multi-fault cases at the end.

cases.name: eighteen-bytes-truncated
cases.note: one byte short; the flags byte is missing

cases.name: twenty-bytes-trailing-zero
cases.note: trailing bytes are a covert channel; strict length is a safety control, not pedantry (SPEC.md §3.1)

cases.name: version-future
cases.note: a v1 device's frame. v0 decoders reject rather than guess.

cases.name: tx-power-zero-dbm
cases.note: 0 dBm is not a plausible calibrated-at-1m value and is not on the legal grid

cases.name: tx-power-off-grid-minus-59
cases.note: -59 dBm is in range but off the 5 dB grid. Rejecting off-grid values closes the byte as a covert channel (SPEC.md §3.2).

cases.name: reserved-flag-bit1
cases.note: the single lowest reserved bit. 7 tolerated reserved bits would be a 7-bit-per-frame covert channel (SPEC.md §3.3).

cases.name: ephemeral-id-all-zero
cases.note: reserved sentinel; what an uninitialised implementation emits (SPEC.md §3.5)

cases.name: multifault-short-and-bad-version
cases.note: length is checked first, so the error is the length error

cases.name: multifault-bad-version-and-bad-tx
cases.note: version is checked before tx power

cases.name: multifault-bad-tx-and-reserved-flag
cases.note: tx power is checked before flags

cases.name: multifault-reserved-flag-and-reserved-eid
cases.note: flags are checked before the ephemeral id
